name: Casper Agentic Buildathon 2026 - Final Round
judging_criteria: Technical execution; innovation and originality; effective AI/agentic use; real-world applicability; user experience; working Casper contracts; launch plans; and long-term impact.
geographic_restrictions: Virtual and globally accessible; an Istanbul workshop was optional rather than a participation requirement.
eligibility_notes: Finalists continued builds from the qualification round. New/original work and a functioning Casper integration were required. No mandatory travel was found.
notes: Headline value was $150,000, but only $30,000 was cash; the remainder was x402 credits and in-kind support. The cash amount is used for the prize-band filter. Several finalists began repositories during the preceding qualification round, so pre-final-round commits are expected and separately recorded.

name: KeeperHub - Agents Onchain Hackathon
judging_criteria: Real onchain execution through KeeperHub; depth of KeeperHub integration; reliability and observability; usefulness and originality; and integration/developer experience. Repositories and claimed transaction hashes were independently reviewed.
geographic_restrictions: Open worldwide and fully virtual; no mandatory travel or in-person appearance found.
eligibility_notes: Every submission had to execute real transactions rather than mocks. GitHub repository and transaction proof were required.
notes: Five announced award recipients are represented: three overall placements and two $500 onboarding-bounty co-winners. DoraHacks displayed 512 registrations and 190 BUIDLs; KeeperHub later described the rounded figures as 500 and 200.

name: BUIDL CTC 2026 Fall - BUIDL For The Real World
judging_criteria: Track alignment and depth of Attestcoin Protocol use; technical execution; originality; product usefulness and feasibility.
geographic_restrictions: Country-of-residence and citizenship information required; detailed legal exclusions not fully published on the page.
eligibility_notes: All work must be original and created during the event. Solo participation explicitly allowed.
notes: Three announced overall winners. Winner sophistication is unusually high; the winning field includes production-like deployments and experienced builders.

name: WTF !! hackathon summer edition
judging_criteria: Originality, technical ambition, working integration with Nox confidential compute, protocol usefulness, execution quality, and potential.
eligibility_notes: Existing integrations may be used if clearly disclosed, but reusing a prior iExec hackathon project was disallowed.
notes: Included because winners were announced in September. Winners are production-like confidential DeFi integrations; this is not a beginner-friendly field despite the small pool.

name: BNB Hack: US College Edition
judging_criteria: Technical execution; originality; real-world relevance; demo and presentation; builder profile; community voting alongside formal judging.
geographic_restrictions: Invite-only for students in registered blockchain clubs at whitelisted US universities.
eligibility_notes: Four-week online event. Public repo, working demo, setup instructions, and BSC onchain proof were required. The later Miami pitch and covered travel were winner benefits, not participation requirements.
notes: Official results explicitly rank three rewarded projects. Registration and estimated-project counts come from Hackathon Radar; the DoraHacks winner page and BNB Chain announcement confirm the three placements. Favorable opportunity structure despite narrow US-student eligibility.

name: Good Vibes Only: OpenClaw Edition
judging_criteria: 40% community voting through DoraHacks upvotes and 60% judging by reviewers with relevant ecosystem context; qualifying entries also required verifiable onchain execution and reproducible code or instructions.
geographic_restrictions: Fully online; no mandatory travel or in-person appearance found.
eligibility_notes: Published rules did not prohibit solo participation or require a multi-person team. Under the canonical rule, solo participation is therefore presumed allowed.
notes: Extended-review band. The organizer planned ten awards but publicly listed nine recipients and reserved the right to withhold prizes; per-winner amounts were not published and are not inferred.

name: Stellar Hacks: ZK Gaming
organizer: Stellar Development Foundation / Build on Stellar
judging_criteria: Meaningful use of zero-knowledge proofs in a core game mechanic; working Stellar testnet integration; functional user interface; reproducible open-source repository; and clear video demonstration.
geographic_restrictions: Online; no mandatory travel or in-person appearance found.
eligibility_notes: Published terms did not prohibit solo participation or require a multi-person team; solo participation is therefore presumed allowed.
notes: Five ranked winners received $5,000, $2,000, $1,250, $1,000, and $750. Organizer announcement dated February 27 provides the complete roster.

name: Kaspathon: Build at Internet Speed
judging_criteria: Originality and creativity 25%; real-world applicability 20%; UX/UI and accessibility 20%; technical implementation 20%; presentation and documentation 15%. Community Favorite was decided separately by community vote.
geographic_restrictions: Online and open internationally, subject to local prize and tax law. Participants under 18 required parent or guardian consent.
eligibility_notes: Terms explicitly allowed teams and solo participants. Pre-existing code was allowed when disclosed and accompanied by significant new work.
notes: Seven distinct projects received rewards. Projects with cumulative main, category, or mention awards appear once with all official placements preserved. The 200,000 KAS pool is recorded as an approximately $10,000 discovery-time value; exact USD award values are not inferred. The exact final-results day was not published, so 2026-03-01 is an approximate Q1 boundary date.

name: Arbitrum Open House NYC Online Buildathon 2026
judging_criteria: Technical execution; product clarity; Arbitrum ecosystem alignment; and long-term project potential.
geographic_restrictions: Global online buildathon. The later NYC Founder House was a separate, in-person follow-on program and was not required to win the online buildathon.
eligibility_notes: No explicit prohibition on solo entrants was found. Projects were expected to make meaningful progress on Arbitrum during the buildathon.
notes: The canonical row covers only the three-week online buildathon and its three published winners. It excludes the later NYC Founder House, whose attendance was in person and whose separate $340,000 awards sit outside the research band.

name: Sui x OpenClaw Agent Hackathon 2026
judging_criteria: Cross-track peer approval voting among shortlisted teams after eligibility screening; the five highest-approved projects in each track received equal $1,900 awards.
geographic_restrictions: Fully online; no mandatory travel or in-person appearance found.
eligibility_notes: Solo participation was not prohibited. Public repositories and transparent AI-development evidence were central to review; twenty-one shortlisted teams participated in the final cross-track vote.
notes: The public winners file awards ten projects equally at $1,900 each. Rankings within each track preserve the published vote ordering; ties are left in published order. The advertised pool was rounded to $20,000, while the explicit awarded total is $19,000.

name: EVE Frontier x Sui Hackathon 2026
judging_criteria: Working integration with the live EVE Frontier environment; technical implementation; utility; creativity; originality; and community voting alongside organizer judging.
geographic_restrictions: Three-week global online event. The grand-prize package included a trip to EVE Fanfest, but travel was a post-win benefit rather than a condition of participation or judging.
eligibility_notes: Solo participation was not prohibited. Entrants needed access to the EVE Frontier builder environment and were expected to deploy mods, Smart Assembly logic, or connected applications.
notes: Extended review completed for the $51k-$100k band. Despite 800+ participants and 120+ projects, the event remained favorable enough to retain: eight distinct reward slots, a $25,000 top package, explicit solo/modder participation, no evidence of bug-bounty agencies dominating the roster, and a 6.7% rewarded-project rate. Established game-domain knowledge raises the technical barrier and is recorded.

name: Kite AI Global Hackathon 2026
judging_criteria: Agent autonomy; developer experience; real-world applicability; novelty and creativity; a functional end-to-end agent that performs a real task and settles paid actions on Kite rather than presenting only slides or a simulation.
geographic_restrictions: Four-week remote hackathon open to builders globally; no mandatory travel or in-person appearance found.
eligibility_notes: Published terms did not prohibit solo participation, so solo entry is presumed allowed. Submissions had to demonstrate an autonomous agent, paid actions, a functional interface, Kite attestations, and a publicly accessible or reproducible demo.
notes: The organizer initially advertised a $10,000 ranked pool, then the official winner announcement documented eight rewarded teams receiving $12,400 in total after three $800 special prizes were added. The final awarded total controls this record. Registration and submission counts were not published.

name: The Notion AI Challenge 2026
judging_criteria: Originality and creativity; technical complexity; and use of the underlying Notion MCP technology.
geographic_restrictions: Online worldwide challenge; the event page explicitly welcomed secondary-school and university students as well as working professionals.
eligibility_notes: No published rule prohibited solo entries. Each of the three selected projects received $500; one winner also received a conversation with Notion co-founder Ivan Zhao.
notes: All three rewarded projects and the equal $500 awards were explicitly identified by MLH. Registration and submission counts were not published.

name: Hackanation 2026
judging_criteria: Platform challenge rules and sponsor track evaluation; exact scoring rubric was not confirmed in accessible event material.
geographic_restrictions: Hybrid event in Brazil; final presentation could be in person or recorded. Geographic eligibility was not independently established.
eligibility_notes: No explicit ban on solo entries found. Official timeline accepts recorded pitch. Zupy describes a nine-year existing business; an existing-project submission received a ranked award.
notes: Official winners list names four Solana projects and three Chainlink projects and awards totaling $6,500; the event headline and original sponsor-prize tab advertise $6,000. Final awarded amounts control the canonical total; sponsor allocation discrepancy requires organizer reconciliation. Seven unique rewarded projects, 43 submissions and 22 finalists.

name: AI Hacker House Solstice Edition
tracks: Crisis Response and Real Time Alerts
judging_criteria: Use of AI, feasibility of the demo, track relevance, and originality; attendees then voted live and the three highest ranked projects received prizes.
geographic_restrictions: One-day in-person event in Porto, Portugal. Travel costs were not assessed for research eligibility.
eligibility_notes: Published rule 7.1 explicitly permits teams or individuals; rule 2 defines a team as 2–5, which does not override individual entry. New AI-powered project built during the event window.
notes: Official prizes €500, €300 and €200. USD values $569, $341 and $228 are rounded using ECB 2026-07-24 EUR/USD reference 1.1377. Official results ranking identifies DocX, Sonder and Wingman as the three rewarded projects; 29 participants and 15 submissions. The platform labels voting points as Raised, not monetary funds.
